job.title: Safety Officer
job.description:
Our client is a well-established commercial construction contractor with a strong reputation for delivering quality projects across WA. With a strong pipeline of work, they are looking to add a Safety Officer to the existing team.

This is a hands-on, site-based role, working across multiple commercial construction projects and supporting Site Managers, subcontractors and the wider workforce to ensure projects are delivered safely and successfully.

You will be someone who enjoys being out on site, building relationships with the workforce and taking a practical approach to safety rather than being stuck behind a desk.

This is a great opportunity for someone looking to join a business where safety is taken seriously and where you will be supported and mentored by an experienced Safety & Systems Manager.

About You:
  • Commercial construction experience
  • Hands-on and comfortable being out on site
  • Trade background with relevant trade qualifications
  • Strong knowledge of WHS legislation and requirements
  • Confident communicating with workers, subcontractors and management
  • Able to work autonomously while also being part of a wider team
  • Strong relationship-building and communication skills
  • Valid driver's licence
  • First Aid Certificate
  • Intermediate computer skills, with MS Office experience preferred
  • Looking for a long-term opportunity with a reputable contractor
Key Responsibilities:
  • Supporting Site Managers with the day-to-day management of health and safety across projects
  • Working closely with the workforce to improve safety awareness and performance
  • Providing coaching, mentoring and practical safety advice to site teams
  • Supporting site inductions and reviewing SWMS and JSAs
  • Monitoring and reviewing safety systems across projects
  • Assisting with incident investigations and ensuring actions are followed through to close out
  • Monitoring subcontractor compliance and worker onboarding
  • Identifying hazards and supporting project teams with effective risk controls
  • Promoting a positive and proactive safety culture across site
This is a great opportunity for a hands-on Safety professional who enjoys being on site and working directly with the workforce.
You will be joining a supportive team with experienced leadership around you, along with the opportunity to work across a variety of commercial construction projects.

A competitive remuneration package will be negotiated based on your experience.

If you're interested in this opportunity, or would like to discuss other potential roles within Health & Safety, click APPLY NOW and register your details.
Alternatively, contact Aaron Walsh via email at awalsh@designandbuild.com.au or on 0412 786 746 for more information.

job.title: GRADUATE ARCHITECTS
job.description:
Join a dynamic architecture practice located in Brisbane where you’ll have the opportunity to work across an exciting and diverse portfolio of large-scale projects spanning multi-residential, hotels, commercial and education.

This is a hands-on role for an architect who enjoys being involved throughout the project lifecycle — from early concept and design development through to documentation, approvals, tender and construction. You’ll work closely with clients and a range of internal and external stakeholders, playing an important role in shaping projects from initial brief through to successful delivery.

We’re looking for an architect who is passionate about design, confident working with clients and stakeholders, and keen to take ownership of projects from concept through to completion.

Key Responsibilities:
  • Engage directly with clients and consultants building strong and collaborative relationships.
  • Develop project briefs, scopes of work and design strategies in response to client and project requirements.
  • Lead and contribute to concept design and design development, working independently as well as collaboratively within a team.
  • Oversee the preparation and coordination of high-quality documentation and specifications through DA, tender, building approval and construction stages.
  • Contribute to a collaborative studio environment, bringing a strong design focus and proactive approach to project delivery.
What you need to be successful:
  • Masters Degree in Architecture
  • 3+ years experience within a professional architecture practice
  • Strong technical capabilities, including Revit, Enscape, Adobe InDesign 
  • Experience working across multi-residential or other large-scale projects.
  • Strong documentation and project coordination skills.
  • A proactive, collaborative approach and genuine enthusiasm for delivering high-quality architectural outcomes.
If you think that you could be a good fit for this position, please apply directly to this add or contact Brittany Steinbach on 0401 205 618 
/ bsteinbach@designandbuild.com.au 
Your application will be treated as strictly confidential.

Thanks for your consideration.

job.title: Contracts Administrator
job.description:
Our client is a well-established and growing specialist contractor delivering complex projects across the construction, infrastructure, government, utilities, transport, resources and commercial sectors.

Due to continued growth and an expanding project portfolio, they are seeking an experienced Contracts Administrator to join their team.

This is an excellent opportunity for a commercially driven Contracts Administrator to join a supportive team and take ownership of the commercial administration across a range of projects.

The Opportunity Working closely with Project Managers and the wider commercial team, you will be responsible for supporting the successful commercial delivery of projects from contract award through to completion.

You will play a key role in managing contractual obligations, protecting commercial outcomes and ensuring projects are delivered effectively and profitably.

Key Responsibilities
  • Administer construction contracts from award through to completion.
  • Review, interpret and manage contractual requirements, notices and obligations.
  • Prepare and manage variations, extensions of time and contractual claims.
  • Assist with subcontractor procurement, negotiation and contract administration.
  • Monitor project costs, commitments, progress claims and commercial performance.
  • Manage payment schedules, invoices and supporting documentation.
  • Maintain accurate contract registers and project documentation.
  • Identify contractual and commercial risks and escalate issues where required.
  • Work closely with Project Managers, site teams and internal stakeholders.
  • Liaise with clients, consultants, subcontractors and suppliers.
  • Assist with monthly reporting, forecasting and project commercial reviews.
  • Ensure contractual and commercial processes are followed across projects.
About You We are looking for a commercially minded Contracts Administrator who enjoys working in a fast-paced project environment and is looking to develop their career with an established contractor.

You will ideally have:
  • Previous experience as a Contracts Administrator within construction, civil, infrastructure or a related contracting environment.
  • A strong understanding of construction contracts and commercial processes.
  • Experience managing variations, claims, EOTs and progress claims.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Excellent attention to detail and organisational skills.
  • The ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
  • Strong stakeholder management and negotiation skills.
  • A proactive and solutions-focused approach.
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in Construction Management, Quantity Surveying, Business, Law or a related discipline will be highly regarded.
Experience working for a subcontractor or specialist contractor would be advantageous.

The Opportunity This is a great opportunity to join a business with a strong project pipeline, established market presence and a reputation for delivering quality outcomes.

You will have the opportunity to work across interesting and technically complex projects while developing your commercial and contractual expertise.

The successful candidate will be joining a collaborative team where initiative is valued and there is genuine opportunity for career progression.

Apply Now with or without a CV or reach out to Jimmy Stewart on 0423 611 276 or jstewart@designandbuild.com.au

job.title: Site Manager
job.description:
A well-established commercial builder with a strong reputation across the ACT is seeking an experienced Site Manager to lead the delivery of landmark commercial projects valued between $20M and $30M.

With a healthy pipeline of secured work and a reputation for delivering high-quality projects, this is an opportunity to join a business that values strong leadership, safety, and quality construction.

As Site Manager, you will take full responsibility for the day-to-day management of site operations, ensuring projects are delivered safely, on programme, within budget and to an exceptional standard. You'll work closely with the Project Manager, subcontractors and client representatives while leading site teams through every stage of construction.

Projects include a mix of commercial developments such as office buildings, education, community, government and mixed-use facilities across Canberra.
Responsibilities

  • Coordinate and supervise subcontractors, suppliers and site personnel.
  • Drive programme and productivity to ensure project milestones are achieved.
  • Maintain the highest standards of WHS compliance and site safety culture.
  • Ensure quality assurance processes are implemented throughout construction.
  • Conduct site meetings and liaise with consultants, clients and project stakeholders.
  • Identify and proactively resolve site issues before they impact programme.
  • Mentor and develop leading hands, supervisors and junior staff.
About You
  • Proven experience as a Site Manager delivering commercial construction projects valued between $20M and $30M.
  • Strong background with a reputable commercial builder.
  • Excellent leadership and communication skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple subcontractor trades simultaneously.
  • Sound understanding of construction methodology, programming and sequencing.
  • Strong focus on safety, quality and client satisfaction.
  • Ability to build positive relationships with clients, consultants and subcontractors.
  • Relevant construction qualifications and current White Card.
What's on Offer
  • Opportunity to deliver high-profile commercial projects across Canberra.
  • Strong pipeline of secured work providing long-term career stability.
  • Supportive leadership team with an excellent industry reputation.
  • Competitive salary package with genuine career progression opportunities.
  • Positive company culture with low staff turnover.
  • Opportunity to work with experienced professionals on technically challenging projects.
If you're an experienced Site Manager looking to take ownership of major commercial builds and join a business known for delivering quality projects, we'd love to hear from you.

For a confidential discussion, contact Sophie Potts at Design & Build Recruitment on 0468 927 182 / spotts@designandbuild.com.au

job.title: AO3 Finance Officer
job.description:
Public Sector People is partnering with a QLD State Government Department to recruit an experienced AO3 Finance Officer for an initial contract running until 27 November 2026. This is an excellent opportunity for a finance professional with strong SAP ECC6 experience to join a busy finance function within a large government agency.

Your Role:
Working within a collaborative finance team, you'll be responsible for the end-to-end processing of invoices, creditor payments, reconciliations, and reporting, ensuring compliance with financial policies, procedures and delegations at all times. This role suits someone who thrives in a high-volume, deadline-driven environment and takes pride in accuracy and process improvement.

Your Responsibilities:
  • Ensure invoices correctly comply with GST and withholding requirements in accordance with financial management standards and authorised by the appropriate delegates
  • Process invoices for payment in accordance with internal controls and financial policies and procedures, investigating any non-compliances
  • Ensure creditors are paid in a timely manner and produce urgent cheques as required by internal stakeholders
  • Enter cheque and travel request claims into the business system and offset them in the finance system when paid
  • Prepare monthly accruals, and maintain and generate recurring and prepayment documents
  • Prepare monthly reconciliations and ensure discrepancies are investigated in a timely manner
  • Investigate overpayments to suppliers and follow up on recovery of overpayments
  • Review corporate card documentation, ensuring correct coding, analysing expenditure, and ensuring compliance with process and policy
  • Liaise with creditors regarding invoices as required, directing other enquiries to the correct personnel
  • Prepare reports for management as required
  • Develop and maintain work instructions for the role
  • Assist staff to action invoices accurately and in a timely manner in the record management system, following up any discrepancies identified
What You'll Bring:
  • Demonstrated experience using SAP ECC6 (essential)
  • Prior experience within a government or public sector finance environment (highly desirable)
  • Strong understanding of accounts payable processes, GST and withholding tax requirements
  • High attention to detail and a methodical approach to reconciliations and compliance
  • Ability to manage competing priorities and meet tight deadlines
  • Strong communication skills and a proactive, team-oriented approach
  • Availability to start immediately
If you're an experienced AO3-level Finance Officer with SAP ECC6 skills and you're ready to start straight away, apply now or reach out to PSP for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Senior Airport Operations & Compliance Coordinator
job.description:
Senior Airport Operations & Compliance Coordinator

Fraser Coast Regional Council | Hervey Bay, QLD | Airport Operations | Stream A Level 6 $104,018 | 9-Day Fortnight | Relocation Assistance up to $6,000

Public Sector People are proud to partner with Fraser Coast Regional Council to recruit a Senior Airport Operations & Compliance Coordinator — a key operational leadership role supporting the safe, secure and compliant operation of Council's airports.

Reporting directly to the Airport Manager, this position will act as a key 2IC within the Airport team, leading an experienced operational team while taking ownership across airside operations, aviation safety, security, compliance and emergency preparedness.

The Role

This is far more than a traditional airport operations position.

You'll play a critical role in ensuring Council's airports continue to meet their operational and regulatory obligations while having the opportunity to make the role your own, establish improved systems and help shape how the airport manages its compliance responsibilities into the future.

A major initial focus will be reviewing and strengthening the airport's compliance framework, ensuring key manuals, procedures and regulatory requirements remain current while establishing a clear ongoing system for managing compliance activities and critical dates.

Working closely with the Airport Manager, you'll lead and support a team of four Airport Operations Officers and an Airport Operations & Business Support Officer, while providing specialist advice across airside operations, safety, security and regulatory compliance.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Leading and coordinating day-to-day airport operations, safety, security and compliance
  • Managing and supporting an experienced airport operations team
  • Maintaining and reviewing the Aerodrome Manual, Transport Security Plan, Airport Emergency Plan and Safety Management System
  • Ensuring compliance with relevant CASA, Department of Home Affairs and other aviation regulatory requirements
  • Establishing effective systems for monitoring regulatory obligations and compliance milestones
  • Coordinating airport risk management, audits, emergency preparedness and compliance reporting
  • Liaising with regulators, airlines, airport tenants, contractors, emergency services and other stakeholders
  • Supporting airport projects, contracts, procurement and capital works
  • Contributing to airport master planning, aviation strategy, asset planning and operational improvement
  • Participating in the airport's on-call arrangements when required
  
The role combines genuine operational responsibility with leadership, governance and continuous improvement, providing the successful candidate with broad exposure across the airport function.

About You

You are an experienced airport operations professional who combines strong airside knowledge with sound judgement, organisation and people skills.

You may already be operating at a similar level within a regional airport, or you could be an experienced Airport Reporting Officer or senior airport operations professional ready to take the next step into a broader leadership position.

Council is not necessarily looking for someone who has spent years in management. More important is your practical airport knowledge, understanding of regulatory requirements and ability to work closely with an experienced operational team while providing the direction and accountability required.

You will bring:
  • Strong experience within airport operations, preferably with well-rounded airside exposure
  • Knowledge of aviation safety, security and regulatory compliance
  • An understanding of CASA requirements and the ability to interpret legislation, standards and regulatory instruments
  • Experience with airport operational manuals, procedures, safety systems or compliance documentation
  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple regulatory requirements and deadlines
  • Leadership experience or demonstrated capability to step into a team leadership position
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills
  • A practical, hands-on approach and willingness to work closely with the operational team
  • Airport Reporting Officer qualifications, or the ability to obtain these shortly after appointment
  • Air Radio Licence, or the ability to obtain one
  • Current driver's licence and ability to obtain an ASIC
  
Strong airside knowledge will be particularly valuable, including practical understanding of areas such as runway conditions, airfield lighting, wildlife management, vegetation, drainage and airside security requirements.

While ARO qualifications are preferred, Council is prepared to consider an exceptional candidate who brings the right broader aviation experience and can obtain the required qualifications shortly after appointment.

Why Join Fraser Coast Regional Council?

This opportunity offers:
  • A genuine 2IC opportunity working directly with the Airport Manager
  • The chance to take ownership of airport operations and compliance and make the role your own
  • Leadership of an experienced and well-established airport operations team
  • Broad exposure across airside operations, safety, security, compliance and airport projects
  • The opportunity to strengthen systems and influence how the airport operates into the future
  • Career progression for an experienced ARO or airport operations professional
  • A 9-day fortnight
  • Relocation assistance up to $6,000
  • The opportunity to live and work on Queensland's Fraser Coast
  
This is particularly well suited to someone currently working within a regional airport who is ready for greater responsibility, or an experienced professional from a larger airport looking for a broader role and a genuine coastal lifestyle change.

You'll join an Airport Manager who is looking for someone who can complement his experience, bring strong airside capability and work alongside him to continue developing the airport function. Most importantly, you'll have the freedom to establish systems, improve processes and take genuine ownership of the position.

Be part of a team responsible for keeping the Fraser Coast connected, while taking the next step in your aviation career.

Apply Now

To apply, please submit your CV and cover letter via the 'Apply Now' button or contact:

Adrian Holder
Lead Search & Select Consultant
Public Sector People
E: adrian@publicsectorpeople.com.au

Applications close: Tuesday 29 September 2026 at 5pm.

job.title: Housing Officer
job.description:
Housing Officer – Tenancy Services

Public Sector People is currently looking for an experienced Tenancy Manager to join an established community housing provider in Queensland.

This organisation provides secure and affordable housing to individuals and families across Queensland. Its approach combines effective tenancy management with early intervention, strong tenant relationships and connections to community support.

This is an opportunity to manage your own portfolio while helping tenants overcome challenges and maintain stable housing.

The Role

You will oversee the full tenancy lifecycle, from commencement and ongoing account management through to property care, complex tenancy matters and exits.

Rather than waiting for issues to escalate, you will work proactively with tenants to understand what is happening, identify practical solutions and connect them with appropriate support. You will balance empathy with accountability, ensuring tenancy obligations are understood and managed consistently.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Managing a portfolio of social and affordable housing tenancies
  • Establishing strong, professional relationships with tenants
  • Monitoring rent accounts and addressing arrears through early intervention
  • Coordinating tenancy commencements, reviews, transfers and exits
  • Responding to property care concerns, neighbourhood disputes and disruptive behaviour
  • Conducting tenant visits and property inspections where required
  • Developing repayment plans and sustainable tenancy strategies
  • Working with support providers, government agencies and internal property teams
  • Preparing notices, evidence and documentation for QCAT proceedings
  • Maintaining accurate case notes, records and tenancy documentation
  • Applying the Residential Tenancies and Rooming Accommodation Act 2008 and relevant organisational policies
About You

You will be comfortable managing competing priorities and making sound decisions in situations that are not always straightforward. You communicate clearly, remain calm during difficult conversations and understand how to combine good customer service with effective tenancy management.

You will ideally bring:
  • Experience in community housing, public housing, residential property management or a related service
  • Working knowledge of Queensland residential tenancy legislation
  • Experience managing arrears, tenancy breaches or complex customer matters
  • Strong negotiation, problem-solving and conflict-resolution skills
  • The confidence to work independently while contributing to a collaborative team
  • Accurate record-keeping and case management skills
  • A current Queensland Driver Licence
Experience working with people experiencing housing instability, financial hardship or other barriers would be highly regarded, as would previous involvement in QCAT matters.

What’s Available
  • Salary packaging benefits
  • SCHADS Award Level 4 conditions
  • Four days working onsite or across the portfolio, with one day from home
  • A supportive team environment with a strong community focus
  • The opportunity to contribute directly to housing stability across Queensland
If you are an experienced housing or property professional looking for a role with genuine social impact, we would be interested in hearing from you.

Apply now or contact Public Sector People for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Development Engineer
job.description:
Development Engineer
Western Downs Regional Council | $107K–$114K + Super | 9-Day Fortnight
  
Looking for a Development Engineering role where you can do interesting technical work without sacrificing your work-life balance?
  
Public Sector People are partnering with Western Downs Regional Council to appoint a Development Engineer to join its planning and development function.
  
This is a broad, hands-on role where you’ll work across subdivisions, operational works, roads, stormwater, flooding and infrastructure planning while helping shape practical development outcomes across a growing regional community.
Importantly, this isn’t an environment where you’ll be buried under an unmanageable DA workload. You’ll join a supportive team with approximately 6–10 DAs per week across the team, alongside a 9-day fortnight and flexible working arrangements.
  
The Opportunity
  
Reporting to the Principal Planner, you’ll provide engineering input throughout the development assessment process, working closely with planners, developers, consultants, internal engineering teams and the wider community.
  
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Assessing development applications and Operational Works
  • Reviewing engineering designs and technical reports across stormwater, flooding and traffic
  • Providing practical engineering advice on subdivisions and development proposals
  • Undertaking site inspections and monitoring compliance with approvals and standards
  • Supporting pre-lodgement discussions with developers and consultants
  • Contributing to infrastructure planning, policy and LGIP matters
  • Working collaboratively to resolve technical issues and achieve sensible development outcomes
  
It’s a varied position where you’ll have the opportunity to influence projects from the early planning stages through to delivery.
  
About You
  
We’re looking for a practical and solutions-focused Civil Engineer who can balance good engineering with the realities of development, planning and stakeholder expectations.
  
You’ll ideally bring:
  • A Degree in Civil Engineering – mandatory
  • Development engineering experience across subdivisions and civil infrastructure
  • Knowledge of development assessment and relevant planning legislation
  • Ability to assess stormwater, flooding, traffic and broader civil engineering matters
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Confidence working with developers, consultants and internal stakeholders
  • A collaborative and pragmatic approach to problem solving
  
RPEQ or progress towards RPEQ is highly regarded, as is previous experience within local government or a consultancy working with councils.
  
Why Western Downs?
  
This is an opportunity to step into a council offering the combination that can be difficult to find in Development Engineering: interesting work, autonomy, flexibility and a genuinely manageable workload.
  
You’ll benefit from a 9-day fortnight, flexible working arrangements and work-from-home options where practical, while working within a stable and supportive team.
  
For someone looking to move away from the pressures of a high-volume metropolitan DA environment—or an engineer wanting broader exposure and greater influence over development outcomes—this represents a strong long-term opportunity.
  
Apply
  
To apply for this role please attach a CV and cover letter using the ‘Apply Now’ function or for further information contact:
  
Adrian Holder
Lead Consultant – Public Sector People
adrian@publicsectorpeople.com.au
  
Applications close: Friday 25th September at 4pm

Pre-Construction Manager
Melbourne, VIC | Permanent Full-Time
 
The Opportunity
Design & Build Recruitment is partnering with a well-established and growing electrical services contractor to appoint an experienced Pre-Construction Manager.
This is a key leadership position sitting at the intersection of Estimating, Design and Operations, taking ownership of projects from early contractor involvement and tender stage through to procurement, delivery planning and operational handover.
 
The role will suit an experienced Project Manager, Senior Estimator, Pre-Construction Manager or Engineer who understands the realities of delivering complex construction projects and enjoys influencing outcomes before construction begins.
With a strong pipeline of major projects and continued business growth, this position offers the opportunity to establish and develop a dedicated pre-construction function, with the expectation that the successful candidate will eventually lead a team.
 
The Role
As Pre-Construction Manager, you will play a critical role in ensuring projects transition effectively from concept and tender through to delivery.
Working closely with senior leadership, estimators, designers and project delivery teams, you will lead ECI and bid opportunities, review major project estimates, identify commercial and technical risks, and develop operational budgets and production metrics ahead of project commencement.
You will remain involved through early design and procurement, ensuring a structured and commercially robust handover into operations.
 
Key Responsibilities
Tender & Estimating
  • Lead and coordinate ECI and major bid opportunities alongside estimating and design teams.
  • Review significant project estimates through to final negotiation stages.
  • Provide input into buildability, constructability and design reviews.
  • Support labour rate build-ups, schedules of rates and standardised estimating information.
  • Provide technical and commercial advice around client budgets, design and project strategy.
  • Support business development activity and major tender opportunities.
Pre-Construction & Project Planning
  • Translate awarded project estimates into operational budgets and production metrics.
  • Undertake detailed reviews of project scope, design and documentation ahead of delivery.
  • Establish and manage project Risk & Opportunity registers.
  • Identify value engineering and design efficiency opportunities.
  • Coordinate early procurement of long-lead and engineered equipment.
  • Lead formal project handovers from pre-construction into operational delivery teams.
  • Coordinate early design engagement with clients and internal design teams.
Project Delivery Support
  • Maintain involvement through early design and procurement stages.
  • Support project teams during the transition into construction.
  • Drive lessons learned and continuous improvement across project delivery.
Leadership & Process Improvement
  • Improve pre-construction processes, systems, templates and reporting.
  • Maintain accurate records across estimates, budgets and handover documentation.
  • Provide reporting on pipeline opportunities, project handovers and key lessons learned.
  • Play a key role in developing the future pre-construction function, with the opportunity to build and lead a team.
About You
We are looking for someone with a strong understanding of the construction lifecycle and the ability to bridge the gap between winning work and successfully delivering it.
You may currently be working as a:
  • Pre-Construction Manager
  • Senior Project Manager
  • Project Manager with strong estimating experience
  • Senior Estimator looking to move closer to project strategy and delivery
  • Electrical or Building Services Engineer with significant commercial project experience
Ideally, you will bring:
  • Experience in project management and/or engineering combined with estimating experience within the construction industry.
  • A strong understanding of buildability, constructability and design review.
  • Experience across the full project lifecycle, from ECI and tender through to design, procurement and project handover.
  • The ability to review complex scopes and identify commercial, technical and delivery risks.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to work across estimating, design, operations and client teams.
  • Experience identifying value engineering and design efficiency opportunities.
  • Excellent analytical, commercial and problem-solving skills.
  • The ability to manage multiple projects and priorities simultaneously.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Experience within electrical services, building services, industrial construction, infrastructure or mission-critical/data centre environments will be highly regarded.
 
What's On Offer?
This is a genuine opportunity to take ownership of a critical function within a growing contractor.
You will have:
  • A highly influential role across major projects.
  • Package: $180,000 - $220,000 + super + vehicle/car allowance (DOE)
  • Exposure to projects from tender through to delivery.
  • The opportunity to shape and improve pre-construction processes.
  • Close collaboration with senior leadership.
  • A clear pathway into building and leading a dedicated pre-construction team.
  • A strong pipeline of complex electrical and infrastructure projects.
  • A permanent, long-term career opportunity with a growing Melbourne-based contractor.
Apply

For a confidential discussion, please contact Connor Gwilliam at Design & Build Recruitment, or apply directly via the link below.
All applications will be treated in the strictest confidence.

About You
We are looking for an experienced traffic and transport engineering professional who can combine technical expertise with strategic thinking and development assessment capability.
  
You will bring:
  • Comprehensive knowledge of contemporary transport planning and design principles, standards, legislation and related disciplines.
  • Significant experience in integrated transport planning, infrastructure strategy, transport infrastructure and development assessment.

  • Strong project and time management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and deliver quality outcomes with limited supervision.
  • Previous experience within Queensland Government, Economic Development Queensland (EDQ), major development or large infrastructure environments will be highly regarded.
  
The Opportunity
This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Traffic/Transport Engineer or Infrastructure Planning professional to influence major development and infrastructure outcomes within Queensland Government.
  
The successful candidate will be more than a technical reviewer — you will be expected to lead complex traffic and transport matters, exercise sound professional judgement, negotiate practical outcomes and provide clear advice that directly supports development and infrastructure decision-making.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance Technician — Sterile Injectables

Location: Chatswood, NSW
Industry: Pharmaceutical Manufacturing (Sterile Injectables)
Hours: Monday–Friday, 8am–4pm (training period), transitioning to rotating 8am–4pm / 7am–3pm shifts
Salary: $100,000–$115,000 + phone + discretionary bonus

 About the Company

Our client is an Australian-owned pharmaceutical manufacturer supplying hospitals nationally and exporting to international markets, with active plans for further global expansion. While smaller than the multinational giants, the business offers genuine access to senior leadership — including regular contact with the CEO — and continued investment in new machinery and cleanroom infrastructure.

This is a business with a strong retention track record: the maintenance team has very low turnover, with tenures ranging from 3 to 20+ years. You'll be joining a close-knit, growing team of 4.

About the Role

We're looking for a hands-on Maintenance Technician to join the site's maintenance team, working across cleanroom and aseptic suite environments supporting liquid filling and sterile injectable manufacturing. This is a step up for someone with tablet/solid-dose maintenance experience looking to move into liquid/sterile processing — or a great fit for someone already working in sterile injectables.

You'll partner closely with a senior technician during onboarding before moving onto the standard rotating roster.

Reporting to: Asset Manager (who reports to the Chief Operations Manager, then CEO)

Key Responsibilities

- Perform preventative maintenance on equipment, critical systems, and services — including purified water systems, cleanroom/aseptic suite systems, vision systems, blister and packaging equipment, and vial-based theatre pack lines (vials sterilised for direct use in operating theatres)
- Attend to breakdowns and troubleshoot faults across equipment, critical systems, and services, escalating to external contractors when a fault is beyond in-house scope
- Investigate and report breakdown root causes and concerns to management
- Ensure adherence to the preventative maintenance schedule
- Document all work and maintain accurate records in the CMMS within a cGMP-compliant change control environment
- Coordinate maintenance and repair activities with external service providers as required

What You'll Also Do

- Follow standard operating procedures in all work performed
- Complete GMP-standard documentation for work activities
- Contribute to the development of procedures and related documentation
- Support investigations into incidents, accidents, quality, and governance issues as needed
- Work collaboratively across Production, R&D, NPI, Validation, and QA/QC to support business objectives
- Identify, assess, and control workplace hazards and risks
- Report any accidents or incidents on the day they occur

 About You

- Mechanically minded, with proven maintenance technician experience in a regulated pharmaceutical environment
- Liquid filling / sterile injectable manufacturing experience strongly preferred; solid dose (tablet) experience will also be considered
- Food manufacturing background is not a fit for this role
- Working knowledge of CMMS platforms
- Exposure to equipment commissioning and validation processes
- Strong troubleshooting and fault-finding skills across mechanical, electrical, or utilities systems (purified water systems, vision systems, packaging lines)
- Comfortable working to GMP/cGMP standards and change control processes
- A collaborative approach and willingness to train and support colleagues
- Strong commitment to workplace health and safety
- No formal pharma qualification required — full training and support provided; the business will also consider candidates straight out of a mechanical apprenticeship


 Why Apply

- Direct, regular exposure to senior leadership including the CEO — a level of access not typical at larger multinational manufacturers
- Genuinely low staff turnover and a stable, tenured team culture
- Ongoing investment in new equipment and cleanroom upgrades
- Structured onboarding alongside a senior technician
- Company-supported training courses (up to $2,000) and career development, including pathways for apprentice-level candidates
- A growing, internationally expanding business with export markets beyond Australia

Interested in learning more? Apply now or reach out for a confidential conversation.

job.title: Senior Interior Designer - Workplace
job.description:
Melbourne | Permanent | Senior-Level Opportunities

We are currently working with two highly regarded Melbourne interior design studios that are looking to appoint experienced Senior Interior Designers to their workplace teams.
While both opportunities sit within the workplace sector, they offer very different environments and project types. Both roles require strong design capability, project leadership and advanced Revit documentation skills.
 
ROLE 1 – Senior Interior Designer | Workplace D&C / Spec Suites Fast-paced workplace design | Design & Documentation | D&C Environment
This is an exciting opportunity to join a design-led business delivering high-volume workplace projects, spec suites and commercial office fit-outs.
The role will suit a Senior Interior Designer who enjoys working at pace, taking ownership of projects and moving seamlessly between concept design, design development and detailed Revit documentation.

The Role
You will be responsible for running multiple workplace projects from design through to delivery, working closely with clients, consultants, builders and internal teams.

You will be involved in:
  • Leading workplace projects from concept through to documentation and delivery
  • Developing workplace concepts, layouts, test fits and design solutions
  • Producing detailed Revit documentation and construction packages
  • Working within a D&C-style environment, responding quickly to project requirements and construction constraints
  • Managing multiple projects and deadlines simultaneously
  • Coordinating consultants and external stakeholders
  • Working directly with clients to understand requirements and develop design solutions
  • Reviewing and resolving documentation, design and construction issues
  • Attending site meetings and supporting projects through delivery
  • Selecting finishes, materials, furniture and fixtures
  • Working closely with project managers, builders and contractors
  • Maintaining a high standard of design quality while working within tight programmes
About You We are looking for someone who is:
  • An experienced Senior Interior Designer with strong workplace experience
  • Highly proficient in Revit with the ability to independently produce detailed documentation
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced D&C or delivery-focused environment
  • Experienced running projects rather than purely contributing to design
  • Confident managing clients, consultants and contractors
  • Commercially aware and comfortable making practical design decisions
  • Organised, proactive and able to manage multiple deadlines
  • Someone who enjoys being hands-on with both design and documentation
This role would particularly suit someone who enjoys the combination of creative design + technical delivery and wants to work in an environment where projects move quickly.
 
ROLE 2 – Senior Interior Designer | Premium Workplace & Wellness Design-led studio | Workplace & Wellness | Team Leadership | High-End Projects

The second opportunity is with a high-end, design-focused interior studio delivering premium workplace, wellness and commercial interiors.
This is a more design-led environment, suited to a Senior Interior Designer who wants to take ownership of projects, lead teams and contribute to the creative direction of significant workplace projects.

The Role
You will take responsibility for projects across the full design lifecycle, from early concept through to detailed documentation and delivery.
You will be involved in:
  • Leading workplace and wellness projects from concept through to completion
  • Developing strong design concepts and design narratives
  • Leading and mentoring junior and mid-level designers
  • Managing project teams and coordinating workloads
  • Preparing presentations and presenting design concepts to clients
  • Developing detailed design and documentation packages
  • Producing and reviewing Revit documentation
  • Coordinating consultants and project stakeholders
  • Managing project programmes, deliverables and deadlines
  • Working closely with clients to understand their vision and requirements
  • Material, finishes, furniture and FF&E selection
  • Supporting project delivery and construction coordination
  • Maintaining design quality and consistency throughout the project
  • Contributing to the studio's broader design culture and creative direction
About You You will ideally have:
  • Strong experience within workplace interior design
  • Proven experience running projects independently
  • Strong conceptual and design development skills
  • Advanced Revit documentation capability
  • Experience leading or mentoring designers
  • Excellent client-facing and presentation skills
  • Strong understanding of workplace design principles
  • Experience coordinating consultants and contractors
  • A high level of attention to detail
  • A genuine passion for high-quality interior design
You don't need to be a traditional "Design Director" to be successful here. The studio is looking for someone who is hands-on, design-focused and capable of taking ownership of projects and people.
 
Which opportunity is right for you? What both opportunities offer Both studios offer the opportunity to work on high-quality Melbourne workplace projects, take genuine ownership of projects and have a significant impact on the finished product.

If you're a Senior Interior Designer who is looking for more responsibility, stronger project ownership and the opportunity to work across design, leadership and Revit documentation, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Structural Engineer
job.description:
Structural Engineer

Looking for a Civil/Structural Engineer for a well-established, niche Consulting Engineering and Building Design firm based in Southern Sydney, with a strong focus on structural engineering.

Our work is predominantly centred around the assessment, investigation and design of existing residential structures, including buildings impacted by fire, tree and vehicle damage, as well as structural defects and remedial works.

We are seeking a motivated and detail-driven Civil/Structural Engineer to join our growing team. This is a great opportunity for an engineer who enjoys structural engineering, wants strong technical exposure and is keen to develop their career alongside experienced senior engineers.

The role is highly structures-focused, with exposure to structural assessment, site investigations, causation reporting, remedial design and structural design across timber, steel and concrete.

Key Responsibilities
  • Undertake structural inspections and assessments of existing buildings.
  • Investigate structural defects, damage and failures and determine causation.
  • Prepare detailed technical and causation reports.
  • Develop scopes of structural and remedial works.
  • Undertake structural analysis and design across timber, steel and concrete.
  • Prepare structural drawings and documentation using AutoCAD.
  • Liaise with clients, contractors and other stakeholders.
  • Work closely with senior engineers and contribute to project delivery.
Skills & Experience
  • Civil or Structural Engineering degree.
  • Experience in structural consulting or building design is desirable.
  • Strong understanding of structural behaviour and engineering fundamentals.
  • Developing or demonstrated capability in timber, steel and concrete design.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent technical report writing and written English.
  • High attention to detail.
  • Proficiency in AutoCAD.
  • Strong communication skills and a willingness to attend site.
  • Genuine interest in developing a career in structural engineering.
Why Join us?
  • Structures-heavy workload with genuine technical exposure.
  • Work across investigation, assessment, remedial and new structural design.
  • Mentoring from experienced senior engineers.
  • 30-week Engineering Seminar Program.
  • Exposure to a broad range of structures across NSW and ACT.
  • Competitive remuneration and performance-based bonuses.
  • Company vehicle provided as part of the remuneration package.
  • Long-term career opportunity within a growing specialist consultancy

We’re recruiting for a Maintenance Technician to join a well‑established residential builder with a strong presence across Perth’s southern suburbs.

This role suits someone with a fixing carpenter trade background who enjoys hands‑on work, problem‑solving, and dealing directly with clients after handover.

You’ll be the go‑to person for warranty and maintenance items across single‑storey homes, ensuring quality standards are upheld and clients feel supported throughout the aftercare process.

What you’ll be doing
  • Completing maintenance and warranty works across new residential homes
  • Handling minor carpentry fixes, adjustments and defect rectifications
  • Coordinating with trades and internal teams to close out jobs efficiently
  • Managing SOR‑based site visits and client communication
  • Maintaining accurate job notes and workflow updates
  • Representing the builder professionally during aftercare appointments
What you’ll bring
  • A fixing carpenter trade background (ideal)
  • Strong understanding of residential construction and finishing standards
  • Good communication skills and a calm, client‑friendly approach
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision
  • Reliable, organised and confident managing multiple jobs
The Offer
  • Up to $95k + Super + Car Allowance
  • Mostly SOR work — consistent, easy-to-plan travel
  • Supportive team and clear processes
  • Stable builder with ongoing work and strong client relationships
  • Flexibility around hours once settled
Ready for a conversation? Zoe Brett – 0481 166 594 zbrett@designandbuild.com.au

job.title: Leading Hand - Tier 2 Builder
job.description:
An opportunity is available for an experienced Leading Hand to join a well-established contractor delivering large-scale high-rise residential apartment projects.

The Role As Leading Hand, you will work closely with the Site Supervisor and Site Manager, playing a key role in the day-to-day coordination of on-site works. You will lead trades on the ground, drive productivity and ensure works are delivered safely, efficiently and to a high standard on a major high-rise apartment development.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Leading and coordinating daily on-site activities across designated work fronts
  • Supervising subcontractors and labour to ensure productivity, quality and safety targets are met
  • Assisting with trade sequencing, site logistics and short-term programming
  • Ensuring all works are carried out in accordance with WHS requirements and site procedures
  • Conducting toolbox talks and contributing to a strong safety culture on site
  • Monitoring workmanship and assisting with inspections, finishes and defect management
  • Supporting the Site Supervisor with reporting and use of site systems such as Hamertech and Procore
  • Maintaining positive working relationships with subcontractors and suppliers
About You:
  • 3+ years’ experience as a Leading Hand or Foreman on high-rise residential apartment projects
  • Strong exposure across structure, fit-out and finishing stages
  • Solid understanding of buildability, sequencing and coordination on complex multi-storey projects
  • Trade background preferred, with the ability to lead crews and manage subcontractors effectively
  • Strong communication skills and a proactive, solutions-focused approach
  • Commitment to safety, quality and teamwork
What’s On Offer / Salary Package
  • Salary: Up to $130k + Super DOE
  • Long-term role with a strong pipeline of upcoming projects, largely based in the same location
  • Opportunity to work on landmark projects valued between $100M–$300M
  • Supportive, team-oriented culture with a strong focus on safety, compliance and quality
If you’re a motivated Leading Hand looking to step into a long-term role with a respected contractor and genuine career progression, this is an excellent opportunity.
For a confidential discussion, please contact Emily Collins at Design & Build Recruitment on 02 9376 8200 or click Apply.

job.title: Contract Administrator

This is a role where you will be closely involved in the commercial management of highly detailed, design-led projects, working alongside experienced Project Managers and Directors in a collaborative, high-performing environment.

The Role

Reporting to the Project Manager and Directors, your responsibilities will include:
  • Managing subcontractor procurement, tendering and letting of trade packages
  • Administering contracts, variations, RFIs and progress claims
  • Supporting cost reporting, forecasting and financial tracking across projects
  • Reviewing drawings and documentation to ensure scope clarity and commercial alignment
  • Liaising with subcontractors, consultants and site teams to resolve commercial matters
  • Ensuring compliance with contract conditions, insurances and project requirements
  • Assisting with project close-out and handover processes
About You
  • Degree qualified in Construction Management, Quantity Surveying or similar
  • 3–5+ years’ experience as a Contract Administrator within residential or commercial construction
  • Experience on high-end residential or boutique apartment projects highly regarded
  • Strong understanding of contracts, procurement and cost control
  • Excellent attention to detail with strong communication and organisational skills
  • A proactive, solutions-focused approach with the ability to work in a close-knit team
In Return
  • Generous salary package depending on experience
  • Work on high-end residential projects
  • Join a boutique builder where quality, craftsmanship and relationships are prioritised
  • Exposure to senior leadership and end-to-end project delivery
  • Long-term career progression within a growing, design-focused business

Please click apply to be considered.

All applications will be treated with strict confidentiality.

job.title: Senior Data Governance & Privacy Specialist
job.description:
Public Sector People are working with the a QLD State Government Organisation based in Brisbane CBD who are seeking a Senior Data Governance & Privacy Specialist to join their organisation on a temporary contract through to the end of March 2027.
  
Lead the development of data governance and privacy frameworks that shape how information is managed across government, using your expertise in governance, stakeholder engagement and privacy impact assessments to deliver practical, high-quality outcomes.
  
Overview:
  
  • Senior Data Governance & Privacy Specialist
  • Start date: As soon as possible
  • Contract through to end March 2027
  • A07 / A08 opportunity - Pay from $87, up to $102 per hour + super
  • Brisbane CBD, Queensland.
  • WFH - hybrid working arrangements available (pending performance and managers approval)
  • Senior specialist / consultant level opportunity
  
What's involved:
  
This is a delivery-focused specialist role that will help strengthen the approach to data governance, open data and privacy management while building organisational capability and supporting trusted information practices.
  
The Senior Data Governance & Privacy Specialist will undertake activities including:
  
Leading the development of data and open data governance frameworks, policies, procedures and associated artefacts.
• Developing governance standards, controls, templates, accountability models, guidance materials and supporting documentation.
• Partnering with information owners, system owners and subject matter experts to understand information assets and business requirements.
• Completing Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs), including privacy risk identification, treatment actions and practical recommendations.
• Supporting compliance with Queensland Government legislation, directives and policies including information privacy, information security and open data requirements.
• Preparing executive briefings, decision papers, status reports and recommendations for senior leaders and governance forums.
• Managing multiple workstreams while providing updates on risks, dependencies and delivery progress.
• Developing practical knowledge content, templates and handover materials to support ongoing capability uplift across the organisation.
  
  
About you:
  
  • Available to commence as soon as possible.
  • Demonstrated experience developing data governance and open data governance frameworks, policies, procedures and supporting governance materials.
  • Strong experience conducting Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs) and documenting privacy risk treatment strategies.
  • Sound understanding of information governance, data management, records management, risk and assurance principles.
  • Previous Queensland Government or public sector experience is highly regarded.
  • Excellent written communication skills with experience preparing executive briefs, governance artefacts and guidance materials.
  • Able to work autonomously, manage multiple deliverables and produce high-quality
  
As an approved Government recruitment partner, Public Sector People are ideally placed to assist you in your search for your next temporary or permanent opportunity.
  
Best of luck!

job.description:
Drafting Manager - Mechanical Services
Dandenong South | $150k - $165k + Super + Vehicle
 
The Company
Our client is a well-established Tier 2 Mechanical Contractor delivering HVAC and mechanical services across a range of major commercial, industrial and infrastructure projects throughout Victoria.
Due to continued growth and an increasing project pipeline, they are looking to appoint an experienced Drafting Manager to take ownership of their drafting function and lead a team of mechanical drafters.
This is a great opportunity to join a growing contractor where you will have genuine influence over processes, systems and the development of the drafting team.
The Role
Reporting into the senior management team, you will be responsible for managing the company's drafting function and ensuring projects are delivered with accurate, coordinated and high-quality mechanical documentation.
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Managing and mentoring a team of mechanical drafters.
  • Overseeing drafting deliverables across multiple projects.
  • Producing and reviewing detailed HVAC and mechanical services drawings.
  • Managing drawing standards, revisions and document control.
  • Coordinating mechanical services with architectural, structural, electrical and other building services.
  • Working closely with Project Managers, Engineers and Site Teams.
  • Assisting with design coordination and resolving construction-related drafting issues.
  • Managing project priorities, deadlines and drafting resources.
  • Reviewing drawings for accuracy, constructability and quality.
  • Supporting BIM/Revit coordination and clash detection.
  • Developing and improving drafting processes, standards and systems.
  • Liaising with consultants, builders and subcontractors where required.
  • Providing technical guidance and support to the wider project team.

job.title: Contract Administrator - Multi-Storey Commercial Construction Melbourne West
job.description:
Truganina | Permanent
The Opportunity
A growing Melbourne-based commercial and industrial builder is looking to appoint two Contract Administrators to support the delivery of new multi-storey projects in Melbourne's western suburbs, with the immediate focus being Truganina.

The business has recently secured a five-storey mixed-use development as part of a broader five-building masterplan. There is also potential for an additional adjacent project of a similar scope.

This represents an exciting period of growth for the business as it continues to expand its capabilities beyond its traditional industrial portfolio and into more complex multi-storey commercial and mixed-use construction.

About the Business
The company is an established Victorian construction and development business with a strong track record across:
  • Industrial and logistics
  • Warehousing and distribution
  • Commercial
  • Office
  • Retail
  • Hospitality
  • Mixed-use developments
They have built their reputation around quality construction, strong client relationships and a hands-on approach to project delivery.
The business has a collaborative and practical culture, with a strong emphasis on teamwork, accountability and delivering quality outcomes rather than operating within a heavily corporate environment.

Why This Role Is Different
The business has traditionally delivered a significant volume of industrial construction, where projects can be relatively straightforward from a commercial and contractual perspective.

The new multi-storey projects introduce a different level of complexity, including:
  • Multiple levels and building interfaces
  • Greater design development
  • Increased consultant coordination
  • More complex subcontractor packages
  • Significant variation and change management
  • More involved services coordination
  • Greater client and consultant interaction
  • Design changes throughout construction
  • Increased commercial and programme implications
As a result, they are specifically looking for CAs who understand how to manage the commercial consequences of change, rather than simply administering straightforward subcontract packages.

The Role
Working closely with the Project Manager and site team, you will take responsibility for the commercial and contractual administration of your project.
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Managing subcontractor packages from procurement through to completion
  • Preparing and administering subcontracts and purchase orders
  • Reviewing subcontractor scopes and quotations
  • Managing progress claims and payment schedules
  • Assessing, negotiating and administering variations
  • Managing EOTs and contractual notices
  • Identifying the commercial impact of design and scope changes
  • Maintaining accurate cost reporting and forecasting
  • Managing RFIs and coordinating with consultants and subcontractors
  • Reviewing drawings, specifications and design changes
  • Supporting procurement and subcontractor negotiations
  • Maintaining project registers and commercial documentation
  • Working closely with the PM to maintain project budgets and programme
  • Supporting the project through to final account and handover
What We're Looking For The ideal candidate will have:
  • 4+ years' experience as a Contract Administrator
  • Strong commercial construction experience
  • Experience across multi-storey commercial, residential or mixed-use projects
  • Strong understanding of variations, EOTs, progress claims and subcontract administration
  • Experience managing design and scope changes
  • Strong procurement and subcontractor management skills
  • Ability to read and interpret drawings and specifications
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills
  • Strong commercial awareness and attention to detail
  • A proactive approach to identifying and resolving issues
If you're a CA looking to broaden your experience into more complex multi-storey construction and want to join a growing builder where you can have genuine ownership of your projects, this could be an excellent next step

job.title: Civil Works Manager
job.description:
Civil Works Manager
North Burnett Regional Council | Mundubbera, QLD | Civil Works & Infrastructure | Circa $150K base + Accommodation + Car allowance
  
Public Sector People are proud to partner with North Burnett Regional Council to recruit an experienced Civil Works Manager to provide strategic and operational leadership across Council's civil works and open spaces functions. This is an outstanding opportunity for a hands-on, visible and people-focused leader who wants to make a genuine difference.
  
This position suits a pro-active leader who will get out across the region, spend time with their teams, understand the condition of the network, visit works in progress and actively resolve the issues that impact employees and the community.
  
With teams operating across six townships, visibility matters. The successful candidate will be expected to build strong relationships with staff, provide clear direction and create an environment where people feel supported, developed and accountable.
  
The Role
  
Reporting to the General Manager Works, you will lead the delivery of Council's civil works services across a diverse regional portfolio encompassing rural and urban roads, bridges, parks and open spaces, aerodromes and cemeteries.
There is a significant opportunity to make your mark.
  
Council is rebuilding momentum across its civil works program, with a strong focus on road renewals, resheeting, resealing and bridge repairs. You'll inherit capable people within the team, while having the opportunity to strengthen leadership, develop emerging talent and improve how works are planned, prioritised and delivered.
  
Key responsibilities include:
  
  • Providing visible, hands-on leadership across geographically dispersed civil works and open spaces teams
  • Leading, coaching and developing staff while building accountability, capability and succession
  • Overseeing the delivery and maintenance of Council's rural and urban road networks and associated infrastructure
  • Developing maintenance programs and identifying renewal priorities through sound asset management practices
  • Leading the planning and delivery of Council's civil capital works program
  • Managing operational and capital budgets and ensuring resources are directed to the areas of greatest need
  • Driving improvements in productivity, plant utilisation, safety and service delivery
  • Working closely with contractors, consultants and internal teams to achieve value-for-money outcomes
  • Building trusted relationships with stakeholders and communities across the North Burnett region
  • Providing clear, consistent and evidence-based advice while following issues through to resolution.
  
The formal position description reinforces this emphasis on visible leadership, staff capability, accountability and safety alongside asset management and capital delivery.
  
About You
  
You are an experienced civil works or infrastructure professional, but importantly, you are a leader who enjoys being involved.
  
You'll be comfortable walking into a depot and talking with frontline employees, visiting a road or project to understand an issue firsthand, mentoring an engineer who wants to progress their career, and then presenting clear and credible advice to senior leadership or elected members.
  
You will bring:
  • Strong experience across civil works, roads, infrastructure maintenance or construction
  • Proven experience leading operational and geographically dispersed teams
  • A hands-on and highly visible leadership style
  • A genuine commitment to coaching, mentoring and developing people
  • Strong asset management and capital works planning capability
  • Sound commercial, financial and project management experience
  • A practical understanding of safety within civil construction and maintenance environments
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to engage equally well with frontline staff, technical professionals, executives and elected members
  • Energy, initiative and a willingness to challenge existing ways of working and implement improvements
  • High levels of integrity, accountability and follow-through.
  
Council is open-minded regarding where you have developed your experience. You may already be working within local or state government, or you may come from civil construction, consulting or another infrastructure environment and be looking to bring your experience into a broader community-focused leadership role. The client specifically confirmed that local government experience is not essential and is interested in candidates who bring energy, ideas and the ability to implement change.
  
A Civil Engineering background and RPEQ would be highly regarded although this is not essential. More important is having the technical credibility to be an informed client and provide sound leadership across the function.
  
Why Join North Burnett Regional Council?
  
This is a role where you can see the impact of your leadership.
  
You'll have the opportunity to strengthen an established team, develop future leaders, rebuild momentum across the road network and introduce new ideas that improve how Council delivers services to its communities. Council sees a genuine opportunity for innovation and more cost-effective delivery as it continues a multi-year program of rebuilding its road network.
  
The package includes:
  • Circa $150,000 base salary
  • $25,000 vehicle allowance
  • Remote locality allowance
  • $5,000 professional development allowance
  • Five weeks annual leave plus leave loading
  • Relocation assistance for the successful candidate
  • Access to Council housing in Mundubbera
  
If you're a civil infrastructure professional who believes leadership means being present, developing your people, communicating clearly and taking ownership of outcomes, this is an opportunity to have a genuine impact across an entire region.
  
Apply Now
  
To apply, please submit your CV and cover letter via the 'Apply Now' button or contact:
  
Adrian Holder
Lead Search & Select Consultant
Public Sector People
E: adrian@publicsectorpeople.com.au
  
Applications close Sunday 20th September at 4pm

job.title: Taxation Compliance and Governance Lead
job.description:
Taxation Compliance and Governance Lead
Noosa Council | Noosa, QLD | $109,838 Base | $124,675 TRP
  
Public Sector People are proud to partner with Noosa Council to recruit an experienced Taxation Compliance and Governance Lead.
  
This is much more than a business-as-usual taxation position.
It is a senior specialist opportunity to lead Council’s response to two critical taxation compliance projects relating to Fringe Benefits Tax and Superannuation Guarantee.
  
Reporting to the Financial Services Manager, you will combine advanced technical taxation knowledge with strong project delivery capability. You will identify and quantify areas of exposure, lead remediation activities and embed governance frameworks that support sustainable compliance beyond the life of the projects.
The role will also provide specialist advice across Goods and Services Tax, contractor classification, supplier taxation obligations and other associated compliance risks.
  
Council needs someone who can do more than identify problems. You will need to translate complex legislation into practical solutions, bring clarity to accountabilities and deliver lasting improvements across finance, payroll, human resources, procurement and governance.
  
The Opportunity
This is a senior individual contributor position with no direct reports. Your influence will come through your technical expertise, judgement, stakeholder capability and ability to lead complex work through to completion.
You will take ownership of the end-to-end delivery of Council’s priority taxation compliance projects, ensuring milestones, deliverables and outcomes are achieved within agreed timeframes.
  
Key responsibilities will include:
  • Leading specialist compliance projects relating to Fringe Benefits Tax and Superannuation Guarantee
  • Acting as Council’s taxation and compliance specialist within Financial Services
  • Providing expert advice across FBT, GST, Superannuation Guarantee, contractor classification and supplier-related taxation obligations
  • Undertaking retrospective compliance reviews, including data analysis, risk identification and impact assessment
  • Quantifying potential exposure and developing practical remediation strategies
  • Designing and embedding fit-for-purpose governance frameworks, policies, procedures and internal controls
  • Partnering with Finance, Remuneration and Benefits, Human Resources, Procurement and Governance teams
  • Clarifying responsibilities and supporting informed decision-making across multidisciplinary teams
  • Managing engagement with external taxation advisers and specialists, ensuring quality, value for money and timely delivery
  • Preparing executive-level briefings, risk assessments, options papers and recommendations
  • Managing project scope, dependencies, milestones and progress reporting
  • Building organisational capability through structured knowledge transfer, clear documentation and practical guidance
  • Ensuring responsibility for ongoing compliance can transition effectively into operational teams at the completion of the projects
  
About You
You will be an experienced taxation, superannuation or compliance professional who is comfortable taking ownership of complex and potentially sensitive issues.
  
You will bring strong technical knowledge, but equally important will be your ability to apply that knowledge in a practical organisational environment. You will know how to move from identifying an issue to quantifying the risk, recommending a course of action and implementing a sustainable solution.
  
You’ll bring:
  • Demonstrated experience leading taxation, superannuation or compliance-focused projects within a large or complex organisation
  • Advanced knowledge of Australian taxation legislation relating to payroll and employment arrangements
  • Strong technical capability across Fringe Benefits Tax and Superannuation Guarantee
  • Knowledge of GST, contractor engagement models and supplier-related taxation obligations
  • Proven experience conducting retrospective compliance reviews and identifying regulatory risk
  • Experience supporting taxation remediation and broader governance improvement initiatives
  • Strong project governance and delivery capability, including managing scope, dependencies, milestones and reporting
  • Experience designing and implementing policies, procedures and internal control frameworks
  • Highly developed stakeholder engagement and communication skills
  • The ability to translate complex legislative and technical requirements into clear, practical advice
  • Strong written capability, including the preparation of executive briefings, risk assessments and recommendations
  • The confidence to work across multidisciplinary teams while maintaining clear advisory and operational accountabilities
  • A practical, solutions-focused approach and the judgement to work through competing risks and priorities
  
You will also hold:
  • A degree in accounting, finance, business or a related discipline, or equivalent demonstrated knowledge and experience in taxation, financial compliance and governance
  • A current C Class driver licence
  
Membership of, or progress towards membership of, a recognised professional accounting body would be advantageous.
  
Previous experience within local government or the broader public sector would be highly regarded but is not essential. Council will also consider candidates from complex corporate environments who can demonstrate the required taxation expertise, governance awareness and project delivery capability.
  
Why Noosa Council?
  
At Noosa Council, being “Different by Nature” reflects more than the region’s location. It represents how Council supports its people, serves its community and protects one of Australia’s most distinctive natural environments.
Based on Kabi Kabi Country, Noosa Shire is home to more than 56,000 residents and covers 872 square kilometres. Internationally recognised as a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, the region offers an exceptional combination of beaches, national parks, lakes and hinterland communities.
Council employs more than 500 people and plays an important role in delivering a sustainable future for the shire.
  
This opportunity offers:
  
  • Full-time, fixed-term employment through to 30 June 2027
  • LGOA Level 6 base salary of $109,838
  • Total remuneration package of $124,675, inclusive of 12% employer superannuation and 17.5% leave loading
  • Applicable salary increases under Council’s Certified Agreement 2025
  • Flexible working arrangements 
  • Five days of Wellbeing Leave
  • Five days of Reproductive Health Leave
  • Employee Assistance Program and workplace wellbeing initiatives
  • Training, mentoring and professional development opportunities
  • The opportunity to deliver meaningful improvements that will strengthen Council’s financial governance and compliance environment
  
This is an opportunity to work where others holiday while delivering complex, high-value work that will have a lasting organisational impact.
  
If you are an experienced taxation or compliance professional looking for an opportunity where you can solve complex problems, lead critical projects and build a stronger governance environment, we would like to hear from you.
  
Apply Now
  
To apply, please submit your CV and cover letter via the “Apply Now” button or contact:
Paul Johanson
QLD State Manager
Public Sector People
E: pjohanson@publicsectorpeople.com.au
M: 0401 857 515
www.publicsectorpeople.com.au
  
Applications close Friday 18 September 2026.
  
Appointment will be subject to Noosa Council’s required pre-employment checks.
